sections.markdown:
## C — Vehicle titling and registration: the title deadline and fees, the MSO and assigned title, out-of-state purchases, odometer disclosure, registering as a resident or new resident, two-year registration, renewal requirements, the notice of sale, stolen or lost plates, and specialty plates
Knowledge domain: when and where to title a vehicle in Missouri and what it costs, which documents prove ownership for new and used vehicles bought in Missouri or elsewhere, what a properly assigned title contains, when an odometer reading is required, how and when to register a vehicle, what renewal takes, and what to do when you sell a vehicle or your plates, tabs or title are stolen, lost or destroyed.

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
Whether you buy a vehicle as a Missouri resident or have just moved to Missouri, you have 30 days to go to a license office and title it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
A title proves that you own the vehicle, and if you do not apply for it within 30 days of buying the vehicle you must pay a penalty fee. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
You can apply for a title at any license office; the title costs $8.50 and there is also a $9.00 processing fee. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
When you title a vehicle you must also pay all the state and local sales taxes that are due. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A01
You receive a receipt when you apply, and the Department later mails you the title. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A01
A title is an important personal document, so do not keep it in your vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A01
Title requirements differ for new and used vehicles and for vehicles bought inside or outside Missouri. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A01
For a new vehicle bought in Missouri, the dealer gives you a title application and an assigned Manufacturer's Statement of Origin, or MSO. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A01
The MSO shows that the vehicle is new and has never been registered. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A01
For a new vehicle, you and the dealer fill in the odometer disclosure on the back of the MSO. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A01
For a used vehicle bought in Missouri, the seller must give you a properly assigned title, and a dealer seller should also give you a completed title application. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A01
An odometer disclosure on the back of the title is required for vehicles of model year 2011 and newer until the vehicle is twenty years old. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A01
If the title assigned to you is from another state, a licensed inspection station must complete an identification number and odometer, or ID/OD, verification form. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A01
For a new vehicle bought out of state, you need the dealer's invoice or a bill of sale plus the assigned MSO from that dealer. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A02
For a used vehicle bought out of state, you need a properly assigned title from the seller or a reassigned title from the dealer. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A02
If the other state does not require a title, you need a bill of sale and the vehicle's last certificate of registration from that state. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A02
A properly assigned title lists the buyer's name and address, the odometer reading if needed, the sale price, the sale date, any lienholder, every seller's signature and printed name, and the buyer's printed name and signature if needed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A02
When a vehicle of model year 2011 or newer that is under 20 years old is sold, the seller writes the mileage on the title assignment. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A02
For a new vehicle, the odometer reading goes on the MSO rather than on a title. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A02
Both the buyer and the seller print and sign their names to confirm the mileage, and sometimes a separate odometer statement is needed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A02
Missouri residents must register their vehicles in Missouri, and a new resident must do so within 30 days of moving in. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A02
A new resident must turn in the out-of-state title and apply for a Missouri title. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A02
If a lender holds your out-of-state title and cannot release it, you provide a statement from the lender saying it will not surrender the title, plus one of three supporting documents. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A03
Registering your vehicle gets you Missouri license plates with a year tab on the plate. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A03
You can register at any license office; a passenger vehicle's fee depends on its taxable horsepower, a commercial vehicle's on its zone and gross weight, and a processing fee is added. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A03
A two-year registration is possible when the year parity matches: an even model year in an even-numbered year or an odd model year in an odd-numbered year; otherwise only one year is offered. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A03
A renewal notice should arrive by mail about two months before your registration expires, but you must renew your plates on time even if it never comes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A03
To be sure your renewal notice reaches you, update your address whenever you move. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A03
To renew you may need the renewal notice, last year's registration receipt or a copy of your title, plus a paid personal property tax receipt or a statement of non-assessment. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-F30 | anchor: A03
Renewal may also require a current insurance card or other proof of financial responsibility and the correct registration and processing fee. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-F31 | anchor: A03
If an inspection applies to your vehicle, renewal needs a safety and/or emissions inspection certificate from the last 60 days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-F32 | anchor: A03
You may be able to renew your plates online, and if you qualify a PIN is printed on your renewal notice. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-F33 | anchor: A04
State law requires you to report selling a motor vehicle or all-terrain vehicle with a Notice of Sale, Form 5049, within 30 days. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec14-F34 | anchor: A04
With a notarized affidavit that they were stolen, you can replace stolen plates and tabs up to two times a year at no cost apart from a $9.00 processing fee. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec14-F35 | anchor: A04
Replacing a lost or destroyed title costs $8.50, plates cost $8.50 per plate, and a set of tabs costs $8.50, each plus a $9.00 processing fee. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec14-F36 | anchor: A04
You may choose personalized or specialty plates, which can carry an extra personalized plate fee on top of the normal registration fee. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

Misconceptions: a title is not something to keep in the glove box; a missing renewal notice does not excuse late renewal; an MSO is for a new vehicle and an assigned title is for a used one; stolen plates are replaced free only with a notarized affidavit and still carry the processing fee; a two-year registration is not open to every vehicle.
Mnemonics: even with even and odd with odd for two-year registration; title in the drawer, not in the car.
Glossary: title means the document proving vehicle ownership; MSO means Manufacturer's Statement of Origin, the new-vehicle ownership document; properly assigned title means a title with the seller-to-buyer assignment area completed; ID/OD verification means the identification number and odometer check done by a licensed inspection station; lienholder means a lender with a claim on the vehicle; year tab means the sticker on the plate showing the registration year.
Dynamic facts: title, plate, tab and processing fees, sales tax amounts, and the online renewal and specialty plate pages can change and must be refreshed from the Department of Revenue.
